- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent 10-day high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10% below recent peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to forecast by subtracting 0.5–1.5x the recent volatility.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates in early days (1–7) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; reduce first 5 days by 1–2% to align with true mean.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead by 0.5–1.0% to capture momentum.
